text:
Jamie Drysdale is playing No. 1 defenceman minutes in Philadelphia. He's up to 24 minutes a night in his last ten games, and all nine of his points this season have come in that stretch, including three assists against Utah and a plus-five night against Minnesota that had Trevor Zegras "flipping out", as one headline put it.

The harder truth is that the Flyers are getting buried with him on the ice. They've had only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five in his minutes, a bit worse than without him, and their shooters have been a little lucky around him. Some of that is the role: big minutes against good players on a team that struggles to keep the puck. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season (0.4 wins), mostly for defence. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on 38% of his entries. At 24 with 94th-percentile speed, the tools are obvious. The defensive results are what decide whether he's a top-pair player.
